title: Node.js (Event Loop, Streams, HTTP, Auth)
description: Event loop phases, streams + backpressure, HTTP servers, middleware, auth, testing. Turing MCQ + FDE coding + Andela pair.

questions.prompt: Which is a phase of the Node.js event loop?
questions.explanation: Phases: timers, pending callbacks, idle/prepare, poll, check, close callbacks. Microtasks/nextTick run between phases.

questions.prompt: `process.nextTick` runs:

options.text: Before any other I/O or timer, after the current operation completes

questions.explanation: nextTick queue drains BEFORE microtasks and any other queue in each cycle. Overuse can starve I/O.

questions.prompt: What is backpressure in Node streams?

options.text: Signal from a slow consumer telling a producer to pause

questions.explanation: `write()` returns false when internal buffer is full; wait for `drain` before writing again. `pipe()` handles this for you.

questions.prompt: Which is the SAFEST way to copy a large file?
questions.explanation: pipe() handles backpressure automatically. readFile buffers the entire file into memory — dies on large files.

questions.prompt: Node ESM vs CommonJS: which is TRUE?

options.text: ESM imports are static and can be tree-shaken; CJS is dynamic

questions.explanation: ESM is analyzable statically. CJS resolves at runtime. Interop rules apply (default vs named).

questions.prompt: What order?
questions.explanation: Sync first (1,6). nextTick queue (3). Microtasks (4). Then macrotasks: timer (5), then check phase (2). setTimeout(0) fires before setImmediate when scheduled from main module (this is unstable, but typical).

questions.prompt: In an Express handler, why is this dangerous?

options.text: Rejections in the async function don't propagate to Express's error middleware unless wrapped
await is not allowed in Express

questions.explanation: Express 4 doesn't handle async errors. Wrap with a helper or use Express 5 / Fastify.

questions.prompt: Which status code is correct for a successful POST that created a resource?
questions.explanation: 201 Created. 202 = Accepted (async). 204 = No Content.

questions.prompt: Which are TRUE about JWT? (select all)

options.text: The payload is base64url-encoded and readable
The signature proves integrity, not confidentiality
You can rotate JWTs without a refresh token
Revoking a JWT before expiry requires server-side state

questions.explanation: JWT payload = base64url + signature. Encrypted variants exist (JWE) but standard JWT is signed only. Revocation needs a denylist / short expiry + refresh.

questions.prompt: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE is designed for:

options.text: Public clients (SPAs, mobile) that can't hold a secret

questions.explanation: PKCE prevents code-interception attacks by binding the code to a per-request verifier.

questions.prompt: Order matters in Express because:

options.text: Middleware runs top-down; auth must come before protected routes; error handlers last

questions.explanation: Registration order = execution order. Body parsers first, auth, then routes, then error handlers (4-arg).

questions.prompt: CPU-bound work in Node should:

options.text: Run inside the main event loop for simplicity
Be offloaded to worker_threads or spawned processes

questions.explanation: Blocking JS on the main thread blocks all I/O. Worker threads share memory via SharedArrayBuffer; child processes don't.

questions.prompt: Why use the `cluster` module or PM2?

options.text: To use all CPU cores by forking worker processes

questions.explanation: Node is single-threaded per process. Cluster forks share the port via master. PM2 wraps this + adds restarts + logs.

questions.prompt: Which package/practice prevents Express XSS via response headers?
questions.explanation: helmet ships secure default headers. CORS handles cross-origin. Morgan is logging.

questions.prompt: Best practice for storing user passwords server-side:
questions.explanation: Adaptive hashing (bcrypt, argon2, scrypt) is slow-by-design to resist brute force. Fast hashes are wrong for passwords.

questions.prompt: An `uncaughtException` in Node should:

options.text: Log + gracefully exit; the process may be in undefined state

questions.explanation: After uncaught exception, process state is unreliable. Log with structured info and exit; supervisor restarts.

questions.prompt: In Jest, `beforeEach` vs `beforeAll` — `beforeEach` runs:

options.text: Before every test in its scope

questions.explanation: beforeAll = once per file/describe scope. beforeEach = per test. Use it to reset fixtures.

questions.prompt: Which best isolates a unit under test that calls a DB?

options.text: Mock the DB module or inject a fake repository

questions.explanation: Unit test = pure logic. Integration test = real DB (usually docker/testcontainers). Don't skip.

questions.prompt: `npm ci` differs from `npm install` in that:

options.text: It requires an exact package-lock.json and never mutates it — used in CI for reproducibility

questions.explanation: `ci` fails if lockfile is out of sync. It wipes node_modules and does a clean install from the lock.

questions.prompt: The `util.promisify` function is used to:

options.text: Turn a Promise into a callback
Convert a Node-style callback function (err-first) into a Promise-returning function

questions.explanation: Classic wrapper. Many APIs now have promise variants natively (fs/promises).

questions.prompt: Given `readable.pipe(a).pipe(b)`, if `b` errors:

options.text: All upstream sources also close automatically
Nothing propagates — you must listen for error on each

questions.explanation: pipe() does NOT forward errors. Use `stream.pipeline()` to get unified error handling + cleanup.

questions.prompt: Write an Express middleware `asyncHandler(fn)` that catches thrown/rejected errors and forwards to next(err).
Write a simple in-memory token-bucket rate limiter middleware `rateLimit({ tokens, refillPerSec })`.
Write `retry(fn, { attempts, baseMs })` with exponential backoff + jitter.
For production logging, best practice is:

options.text: Structured JSON logs (pino/winston) with levels, correlation IDs, and shipped to a store

questions.explanation: JSON is queryable. Correlation IDs tie logs across services. Ship to Loki/CloudWatch/Datadog.

questions.prompt: A CPU-heavy sync function inside a request handler will:

options.text: Run on a worker thread automatically
Block the event loop — ALL concurrent requests wait, latency spikes across the app

questions.explanation: Node is single-threaded for JS. Offload CPU work to worker_threads or split into `setImmediate` chunks.

questions.prompt: Preferred way to compose streams safely in modern Node:

options.text: `stream.pipeline(a, b, c, err => ...)` — propagates errors + cleans up

questions.explanation: pipeline handles error propagation + auto-destroys sources; also has `pipeline.promises` for await.

questions.prompt: For a 10GB file → gzip → S3 upload, memory-efficient approach:

options.text: createReadStream → pipeline → zlib.createGzip → S3 upload stream (multipart under the hood)

questions.explanation: Constant memory — bytes flow through. AWS SDK v3 accepts a Readable in the Body.

questions.prompt: Fastify vs Express key advantage:

options.text: Native async handler support, JSON schema-based validation + serialization, faster throughput

questions.explanation: Fastify treats async as first-class + JSON schema saves cycles on ser/de. Express is still simpler for tiny apps.

questions.prompt: For a Node HTTP client, connection pooling / keep-alive is critical because:

options.text: TCP + TLS handshake per request adds 100+ms; pooling reuses connections, cuts latency + resource cost

questions.explanation: undici (Node's native fetch backend) pools by default. axios/got need explicit agent. Set `keepAlive: true`.

questions.prompt: Rotating a JWT signing secret across a fleet without logout:

options.text: Publish JWKS with multiple public keys; issue with new key; verifiers accept any listed key; old key retired after old tokens expire

questions.explanation: kid (Key ID) header in JWT tells verifier which key to use. Standard rotation flow across auth0/cognito/etc.

questions.prompt: Preventing prototype pollution in a JSON-accepting API: (select all)

options.text: Use `Object.create(null)` for maps that will merge user input
Use a schema validator (Zod/Joi/Ajv) that strips unknown keys

questions.explanation: Merge/deep-set operations are the vector. Real bugs: lodash.merge, express-fileupload CVEs. Layer defenses.

questions.prompt: Best pattern for reading environment config in a typed way:

options.text: Validate + parse env at boot with a Zod/Joi schema; export a typed `config` object; fail fast on missing/invalid

questions.explanation: Untyped env leaks strings-as-numbers bugs. Fail-fast at boot is better than runtime NaN.

questions.prompt: Test-database strategy for integration tests:

options.text: Ephemeral DB per test run (Docker via testcontainers), migrated at startup, truncated between tests OR wrapped in a rolled-back txn

questions.explanation: testcontainers-node spins Postgres/Redis on demand. Rollback-per-test is fastest.

questions.prompt: On SIGTERM, a well-behaved Node HTTP server should:

options.text: Stop accepting new connections, drain in-flight requests within a timeout, then exit — enables zero-downtime rolling deploys

questions.explanation: `server.close()` + finish outstanding work. K8s sends SIGTERM before terminating the pod.

questions.prompt: A Transform stream should call `callback(null, chunk)` when:

options.text: After it's done processing THIS chunk and has produced output (or produced nothing but is ready for more)

questions.explanation: Callback signals 'ready for next chunk' — key to backpressure. Errors pass as first arg.

questions.prompt: For a stateless HTTP service on a 16-core machine, typical worker count is:

options.text: ~16 (one per core), fronted by cluster module or PM2 or an orchestrator like K8s with pod-per-core

questions.explanation: Node's JS is single-threaded per process — need ~1 process per core to use CPU. In K8s, one process per pod, cores per pod tuned via limits.

questions.prompt: Sharing large data between worker_threads without copying:

options.text: Use SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics for shared memory; or transferable ArrayBuffer for zero-copy handoff

questions.explanation: SharedArrayBuffer needs COOP/COEP headers in browsers. Node just works. Atomics for synchronization.

questions.prompt: Sync FS methods in a request handler:

options.text: Block the event loop — never use `readFileSync` in a request path, only at startup

questions.explanation: Any sync I/O in request path stalls all concurrent requests. `fs/promises` for everything hot-path.

questions.prompt: Adding OpenTelemetry to a Node service typically:

options.text: Auto-instruments popular libs (http, express, pg, redis) via `require`/`import` hooks; manual spans for custom code

questions.explanation: `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node` = zero-config traces for common libs. Export to Jaeger/Tempo/Datadog.

questions.prompt: Prisma advantage over Sequelize:

options.text: Generated types from schema → full TS type-safety on queries; explicit relations; migrations as SQL diff

questions.explanation: Codegen-based type safety is the killer feature. Downside: transaction API is more restrictive; escape hatches to raw SQL for complex queries.

questions.prompt: For a Node monorepo, pnpm/yarn/npm workspaces solve:

options.text: Shared dependencies + local package linking + one lockfile — replaces the old lerna+npm-link dance

questions.explanation: pnpm is fastest + strictest. Turborepo/Nx add task caching on top.

questions.prompt: Preventing Slowloris-style attacks on your Node HTTP server:

options.text: Set `server.headersTimeout`, `server.requestTimeout`, `keepAliveTimeout`; put a reverse proxy (nginx/Cloudflare) in front

questions.explanation: Default Node timeouts are lenient; explicit values close half-open attackers. RP in front absorbs most attack surface.

questions.prompt: Best Redis client pattern for high-throughput Node service:

options.text: Single shared client (ioredis) reused across the process; enable pipelining; use cluster mode client for Redis Cluster

questions.explanation: Redis is single-threaded — one TCP connection with pipelining is often faster than many. cluster mode client handles slot routing.

questions.prompt: A background job triggers on webhook. Same webhook fires 5x fast (network retry). Preventing duplicate processing:

options.text: Use idempotency key (from webhook headers) stored in DB with unique constraint; INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; skip if already processed

questions.explanation: DB unique constraint is the atomic gate. Distributed lock via Redis is a weaker alternative.

questions.prompt: For a small production Node Docker image, best base:

options.text: node:20-alpine or distroless, multi-stage build to drop devDeps + build tools

questions.explanation: Alpine has smaller image; distroless has less attack surface. Multi-stage keeps final image lean.

questions.prompt: `AsyncLocalStorage` in Node is useful for:

options.text: Carrying per-request context (correlation ID, user) implicitly across async boundaries without threading it through every function

questions.explanation: Built on async_hooks. Every logger/tracer library uses it under the hood.

questions.prompt: Write an idempotency-key Express middleware backed by Redis (skip processing if key seen in last 24h; return cached response).
Write a WebSocket broadcast helper: `broadcast(room, message)` that sends to all sockets in a room across N app instances (Redis pub/sub backbone).
Write `streamNdjson(url, onRow)` that fetches a large NDJSON endpoint and processes rows as they arrive without buffering the whole body.
